# Liberal Democrats 2019 Manifesto Summary

## Core Vision
The Liberal Democrats' 2019 manifesto centered on three fundamental goals: stopping Brexit, tackling the climate emergency, and investing in public services. The party positioned itself as the strongest Remain party, arguing that EU membership provides economic benefits worth a "£50 billion Remain Bonus" to invest in schools and reducing inequality.

## Key Economic Proposals
The party proposed investing £130 billion in infrastructure including transport, broadband, homes, and green technology. They pledged to introduce "Skills Wallets" giving every adult £10,000 for education and training throughout their lives. Their economic vision emphasized innovation, entrepreneurship, and regional rebalancing through a £50 billion fund for infrastructure across UK nations and regions.

## Climate and Environment
Liberal Democrats committed to reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2045. Key pledges included generating 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030, insulating all UK homes by 2030 to end fuel poverty, banning fracking, planting 60 million trees annually, and ensuring all new cars are electric by 2030.

## Education and Health
In education, they proposed reversing school funding cuts, hiring 20,000 additional teachers, and providing free childcare from nine months for working parents. For health, they pledged to raise income tax by 1p to generate £7 billion annually for NHS and social care, with particular focus on transforming mental health services to achieve parity with physical health treatment.

## Social Justice and Immigration
The manifesto emphasized building 100,000 social homes annually, ending rough sleeping within five years, and reforming Universal Credit. On immigration, they pledged to scrap the "hostile environment" policy, introduce a 28-day detention limit, and welcome 10,000 refugee children over ten years.

## Political Reform
The party advocated for proportional representation, votes at 16, and a federal UK structure with greater devolution to Scotland, Wales, and English regions.
